transcript.content: Hello, thank you for coming in. Can you tell me what’s been bothering you or what brings you here today?

I guess they brought me in because at the warehouse I keep doing things... like, freezing with my arms up by the forklift. It's just... the forklift is yellow, you know? Like a school bus. I used to ride the bus with this kid who always had a yellow lunchbox, and he would trade me his fruit snacks. But yeah, at work, I copy the beeping sounds the machines make, and the hand signals. And I move the boxes in these strange little patterns. Even when everyone is yelling for me to stop. They yell a lot. My dad used to yell when the football game was on, especially if the team in blue was losing. Blue's a good color, though. It's like the sky before it gets totally dark. But yeah, the boxes... they just have to be in the patterns.
Do you often find yourself repeating sounds or copying other people's movements without meaning to?

Well, yeah, like I was just saying about the warehouse... I don't really plan it, it just happens. I'll just be standing there frozen, or my mouth just starts making the backup beeps when the trucks move. And I copy the guys waving their arms to guide the pallets. Waving arms... it's kind of like those big inflatable tube guys at car dealerships, you know? There was a huge red one right down the street from my dorm when I was taking classes. Red fades so fast in the sun, though. Sun damage is terrible for clear coats on cars. My roommate had this old Honda and the paint on the hood was totally peeling off. We tried to buff it out once in the parking lot, but you can't really buff out peeling paint. You need a whole new base coat if you want it to look right. But yeah, the beeping.
Do you find yourself doing these same kinds of things—like repeating sounds or copying movements—outside of work, or does it mostly happen at the warehouse?

I mean, I don't really know. I guess I haven't noticed it outside of work, or maybe no one's yelled at me about it yet. But at the warehouse, it's just so loud, you know? The beeping is everywhere. Beepers are weird little devices. My uncle used to carry a pager back in the nineties. It was this little black plastic box that just clipped to his belt, and he'd always have to find a payphone when it went off. Payphones are completely gone now. It's kind of sad, really. I remember there used to be one outside the diner near my house, and the receiver always smelled like stale smoke and old pennies. Pennies are practically useless now, they cost more to make than they're worth. I read somewhere they were going to stop minting them, but I guess they never did. But anyway, yeah, I don't think I do it at home.
Outside of the warehouse, do you ever feel like your thoughts or behaviors make it hard to connect with people, like maybe you're not understanding social cues or people don’t understand you?

I mean, yeah, I guess people don't really get what I'm saying a lot of the time. Like... when my supervisor asks me which pallets are going on the truck, I really try to explain it to him. But my words just start jumping all over the place. I'll start talking about the load sheet, and then suddenly I'm talking about my old house. The siding on that house was this weird green color, almost like pond scum. And then I'm talking about fishing... fishing is mostly just waiting around anyway, staring at the water. The water gets so murky in the summer when it doesn't rain. And then I just jump to talking about the wooden donation boxes at my church. 

So by the time I'm actually done talking, nobody has any clue what I meant or what pallets are supposed to go where. Pallets are made of such cheap wood, too. If you don't wear thick gloves, you get these massive splinters. I had a splinter once that got totally infected because I tried to dig it out with a safety pin. Safety pins are actually super useful to keep in your pocket, though. You never know when a button is gonna pop off your shirt.
Have you ever experienced sudden and intense changes in your mood, like going from feeling fine to extremely irritable, sad, or excited without a clear reason?

I don't really know about sudden changes. I mean, sometimes I guess I feel okay and then I just... don't. But it's not like a big dramatic thing, you know? It's more just like... standing there. Standing is actually really bad for your lower back if you don't have the right shoes. My dad always used to tell me to invest in good boots. He had this pair of Red Wings that he wore for like, fifteen years. They were so scuffed up they didn't even look brown anymore, just kind of gray and cracked. Leather cracks so easily if you don't oil it. I bought some mink oil once for a baseball glove I had. Baseball is such a slow game, honestly. I went to a minor league game once and it went into fourteen innings. The lights at the stadium were buzzing so loud by the end of it. Bugs always swarm those big halogen lights... they just fly right into them. But yeah, I don't really know about my mood changing all that much.
